summary:
TERRA-MARS Planetary Analog Finder is a bilingual (English/Arabic), non-compensatory geospatial similarity engine designed to identify and validate Earth locations that mirror Martian and Lunar environments before launch. Traditional visual comparisons or simple averages allow a high score in one metric to mask fatal terrain hazards. To solve this, TERRA-MARS integrates real orbital datasets—NASA MGS MOLA, MGS TES, and NASA SRTM—across 400 verified elevation points to evaluate any latitude/longitude or custom CSV dataset.

Our four-layer model scores sites against Martian targets like Noachis Terra Crater using objective CRITIC-method weights: terrain ruggedness via Wasserstein-1 distance (35.36%), basaltic/plagioclase mineral spectra (34.49%), and thermal inertia with surface temperature (30.16%), enforced by a strict safety veto that zeroes operational scores when slopes exceed 10° for landers or 15° for rovers.

Testing Egyptian sites revealed Farafra Depression (84.1%) as optimal for lander safety, the Black Desert (82.3%) for rover navigation, while vetoing Gilf Kebir’s 18.59° escarpment (0.0%), accelerating reliable, data-driven mission readiness on Earth.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

TERRA-MARS Planetary Analog Finder is a bilingual (English/Arabic), non-compensatory geospatial similarity engine that evaluates how closely terrestrial sites match Martian and Lunar environments before launch. Users can scan any latitude/longitude coordinate, select verified benchmark sites, upload custom CSV elevation datasets, and export a complete technical dossier. Across 400 verified elevation points, the engine scores candidates against targets such as Mars' Noachis Terra Crater (-29.41° S, 1.38° E) using four layers weighted objectively via the CRITIC method (validated under ±10% and ±20% sensitivity tests):

1. Terrain Shape (S_morph — 35.36%): Compares full slope distributions and surface ruggedness using the Wasserstein-1 (W1) distance.

2. Mineral Composition (S_spec — 34.49%): Matches mafic and basaltic rock using MGS TES plagioclase abundance.

3. Thermal & Regolith Properties (S_thermo — 30.16%): Combines thermal inertia with surface temperature in Kelvin.

4. Operational Safety Veto (G_veto): Enforces a strict hard limit that zeroes operational scores (0.0%) if maximum slope exceeds 10° for landers or 15° for rovers.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Traditional visual comparisons or simple weighted averages allow a high score in one metric to mask fatal terrain hazards. Applying TERRA-MARS to Egyptian analog sites demonstrated clear mission-planning impact: Farafra Depression achieved 84.1% (5.38° max slope, 94.96% thermal match) as the safest lander analog; the Black Desert scored 82.3% (9.18° max slope, W1 = 0.476°) for rover navigation; while Gilf Kebir Plateau was vetoed for landing (0.0%) due to its 18.59° escarpment despite a 79.11% whole-crater geomorphology match. This helps space agencies and researchers select safer, cost-effective Earth testbeds.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

Developed as an interactive web platform using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, geospatial mapping libraries, elevation/slope profile charts, CSV data parsing, automated technical dossier generation, and Google Sites web embedding, supported by AI tools for code structuring and scientific documentation.

Creativity & Factors Considered:

Beyond non-compensatory safety gating, our team explicitly modeled where Earth analogs hold versus where they break—accounting for differences in gravity (9.81 vs. 3.72 m/s²), atmospheric pressure (1013 mbar N2/O2 vs. 6.1 mbar CO2), Martian frost cycles, and cosmic radiation—providing clear recommendations on when field tests must be paired with environmental chamber simulations.
